items.question: Is Block C (BLD_C anchor plus every C-relative SITE/INT item) misplaced, or are the Hall-C passage, A_W and A_N items misplaced, and by how much (dx, dy)?
items.decision:
Block C and all of its C-relative items are misplaced. The passage and Hall are not. A_N/A_W north ends are also misplaced.
(a) BLD_C.json anchor.world_xy [173.264,-3.64] -> [176.364,-0.14]; x_dir unchanged. New world corners: SW (176.364,-0.140), NW (177.153,19.644), SE (205.792,-0.013), NE (206.581,19.772). Rewrite the anchor.status note: the Google offset is not lean (low C items show it too).
(b) Translate every C-relative world-coordinate item by (+3.10,+3.50):
- SITE_CPlaza.json: all elements, including the TreeAN/PlanterAN/BenchAN rows, PlanterE_Ramp and JuniperE_Ramp.
- SITE_CPlaza_Props.json: all 4 elements.
- ground_surfaces CPlaza and CEast_Lot: move the north edge (C side) and the west edge x 172 by (+3.1,+3.5); move the south edge with A_N, see (d).
- INT_C_Basement / INT_C_F1 / INT_C_Floors: regenerate with C_ORIGIN = [176.364,-0.14] in Scripts/Geo/zones/zone_c_v6.py, and the same constant in zone_c_basement.py and c_shell_v6.py. Do not hand-edit the generated files.
(c) BLD_C.json attachments WestShed (edge 8): keep the shed's west front and north end where they are in the world. depth 5.8 -> 8.9; u0 -1.3 -> +1.3 (+-0.5); u1 19.35 unchanged. The Google navy strip x 173.6-176.3 is the shed's upper roof, not C's facade.
(d) BLD_A_N.json ring: north vertices [35.2,73.2],[10.9,73.2] -> [35.2,77.5],[10.9,77.5]. BLD_A_W.json ring: [10.9,72.95],[4.5,72.95] -> [10.9,77.25],[4.5,77.25]. This reverts the 2026-09-27 3.3 m south move plus 1.0 m. New A_N NW corner (173.527,-15.872); A_W NW corner (167.121,-15.808). Edge-2 facade items follow automatically.
(e) SITE_Garden.json AW_NorthRamp, AW_NorthRamp_Base, AW_NorthRampRail_W/E (and the AW_NorthSteps set) move by +4.3 along the A y-axis = (+0.21,+4.30).
(f) SITE_HallCPassage items (ramp, landing rail, stair, Shed_Apron, Shed_Apron_Kerb, ShedLedge) do not move. For the coping, upper lawn and lamp see D1-01.
items.methods:
M1, Google z20 ortho (0.1 m/px), ground or low features, using passage items as the reference.
- The passage ramp (156.2-157.3, 6.8-10.6) and landing rail (y 7.8) match the model within 0.2 m. The shed's west front is at x 168.0-168.3 (model 167.5).
- Low C-attached items are offset from the model. SW basement-entry canopy (2.4 m high): east end x 176.4 (model 173.29), south edge -2.7 (-6.69), north edge 0.6 (-2.84). So dx +3.1, dy +3.4..+4.0.
- Entrance canopy (5 m high): x 189.8-193.8 (model 185.7-190.1), front -4.6 (-7.7). So dx +3.9 raw, dy +3.1 raw.
- C roof colour profiles: eaves at x 176.7-207.2 and y -2.5..18.1, roof centre offset (+3.6,+1.4) raw.
- Low items versus roof give lean_x ~0 and lean_y ~-0.2 m/m. That puts C at ground at about (+3.1, +3.4..+4.2).
M2, C-frame photo cameras (verify2_1: t31, A028, A031; Q2-13 CC015/016).
- The passage appears (-2.5+-1, -4.1+-0.6) relative to C. Decomposed with the Google coping at -1.4 (D1-01), this gives C dy +2.7..+4.1 and dx +2.5.
- After the shift, the A028 camera leaves the inside of HallEast and lands on the passage landing, and the A031 spruces move to the frame edge (verify2_1 note).
M3, CE024 group bundle (gpnp.py, ce024.py).
- 15 C surround corners and the pilaster edge, plus the A_N NW-corner vertical, the plinth-top line (z 6.65) and, optionally, F2-window lines. f 2780/2840/2900.
- The 0.25 m A_N/A_W step is visible at px x 2920.
- C relative to A_N: dx +2.7..+3.4 (+-0.3..1.5); dy -0.4 with the window lines (rms 9) or -1.6+-0.6 without them (rms 3.5).
M4, eave gap between the C south eave and the A_N north eave at x 178-184, in all three orthos: Google 13.6, Bing 12.5, Esri 13.65, against 15.26 in the model. Corrected for lean, this is 1.0-2.0 narrower, which agrees with M3. The A_N north eave is +3.6 raw in Google/Esri, about +5.5 with the lean correction. Combined: A_N +4.3+-1.0.
items.error: C: dx +3.1+-0.4, dy +3.5+-0.8 (methods spread from +2.7 to +4.2). A_N/A_W north ends: +4.3+-1.0. Passage ramp/rail: 0+-0.2.
items.confidence: high that C is the misplaced block (4 methods); medium on the size of the shift; medium-low for the A_N/A_W north-end amount (Q2-13 alone would keep A_W's north end, but it is low weight: rms 11.7 and an implausible camera height)
items.what_would_settle: To refine the magnitudes: one tape from C's SW corner to A_N's NW corner (model after the change: 15.7 m N-S), plus one tape along the shed front from the shed's north end to the coping/lamp junction.

items.question: B-corner wide stair versus the pergola-walk east end: where is the stair, and what is its geometry (an L-stair with a west-facing lower flight?)
items.decision:
The stair is about 4.8 m north of the model. Its foot is directly at the walk's east end. It is not an L-stair: it is one north-facing flight whose lower steps wrap round the west end. Do not move the walk.
SITE_GateAlley.json: replace Steps_BCorner_Upper and Steps_BCorner_Lower with a single stairs_run 'Steps_BCorner':
- top [155.90,-49.88], dir_deg 87.192 (downhill north)
- risers 7 (6 granite plus the grey concrete top kerb), riser_h 0.1743, z_top 6.57 (total 1.22)
- tread 0.30, width 7.2
- bottom riser line from (152.30,-47.90) to (159.50,-48.25)
West end: steps 1-2 run on west past the return wall to x 152.30 / 152.60, with west-facing ends. Steps 3-7 die into RetainingWall_South_Return; its line starts at the stair: [[152.0,-48.6],[151.34,-53.25]].
East end: stepped back 0.30 per tread beside the red-tile planter cheek (A134), outer edge x ~159.5.
SITE_Garden.json:
- Cut PergolaEast_Landing_N/S/E so the lower (5.35) landing ends at the bottom riser (y > -48.1).
- Raise the area from y -49.9 to -55.2 (x 152-159.6) to the alley level, 6.57.
- Delete the old upper flight footprint.
This contradicts the owner's 2026-09-28 screenshot instruction ('moved back 3.05 m, top on the BBed_Conifer_01 line'); a human should confirm it.
items.methods:
M1, Google z20 luminance profiles: a granite band at y -47.5..-50.0 over x 152.5-159.6 (at y -48.5 the west edge dip is at 152.6-152.9), with paving north of it. The stair's top-kerb nosing is predicted at -49.88.
M2, pergola-frame PnP (A147, A154): bottom riser y -47.9, west end x 152.3+-0.2.
M3, A141 gallery-frame PnP: the bottom riser at -53.75 comes from a one-bay (5.89 m) misidentification of the gallery posts. Corrected: -53.75+5.89 = -47.86 (x 158.4-159.7). The same correction fixes X3-09.
M4, A212 (gallery frame, consistent): flat upper plaza from the south to y ~-51, so the top edge is -50..-51.
Geometry: A129 metrology (12 edge rows, pavers at 1200 px/m): 6 granite risers 0.166, tread 0.30. 012404116 and A150: plus the concrete kerb riser, 7 in all. A145: boulder wall meets the stair at step 3-4. A129 image: the bottom step runs on west past the wall.
items.error: Bottom riser y +-0.3 (the 3 methods agree within 0.4); west end x +-0.2; treads +-0.03; end staggers +-0.3
items.confidence: medium-high for position; medium for the end details
items.what_would_settle: Owner confirmation, because this conflicts with the 09-28 instruction. Optionally a tape from the first pergola hoop's south leg to the bottom riser's west end.

items.question: Are the A_W west-face window surrounds about 1.25 m south of the gallery posts?
items.decision: No change to BLD_A_W.json facades[edge 3] windows u or posts_u. There is no uniform 1.25 m shift. New observation (see D1-02): in the A137 bays, the window spacing is 4.85 m, not 5.89.
items.methods:
M1, A137 wall-plane PnP (a137.py): two window frames, 1.87 x 1.36 (A228-checked), rms 3.2 px, f 2780-2900. Post-foot rays onto the deck plane (frame bottom -0.97). The north post is +0.07 from window 1's centre; the south post is 0.62 south of window 2's centre; post depth 2.93. With the depth fixed at 2.2: -0.43 / +1.11.
M2, A154 (pergola-hoop frame, rms 3.6) gives +1.25 for Sur_E3_04 only. That camera frame belongs to the stair dispute (X3-03), so it gets low weight. The offset may still be real in that one bay if the spacing is irregular.
items.error: Post vs window centre: -0.4..+1.1 per bay (+-0.15 each)
items.confidence: medium (that there is no uniform shift); low (per-bay offsets)
items.what_would_settle: A tape from each post centre to the nearest surround edge in 3 bays (north, middle, south), or one frontal walk-along video of the gallery.

items.question: What is the plaza paving level in front of the C west wing relative to C (PnP says ~0.45 lower; the entrance has 7 x 0.154 risers)?
items.decision:
The plaza in front of the C west wing is lower than modelled; there is no datum error in C. The plaza falls about 0.27 m westward.
Plaza grade south of edge 0 (C-local u 0..8, v -1..-7): z 5.05 (FFL-1.35). Rising linearly to 5.32 (FFL-1.08) at the entrance-stair foot (u 12.8). Set this in the terrain pad / SITE_CPlaza ground under the CPlaza ring.
LightwellCover_E0 outer bottom edge and the W-row planters (PlanterW_S0..W_3, curb_h 0.08) sit on 5.05.
BLD_C ffl_z 6.4 and the entrance stair are unchanged.
items.methods:
M1, CE030 joint fit (ce030.py): C-frame surround corners plus 4 juniper pits as 1.2 m squares aligned with C, with unknown centres and kerb top = zp+0.08. Plaza 5.05+-0.05; rms 7.4; f-insensitive. The prior CE030 F3-bottom picks were about 50 px off and are re-picked. Column-1-only fit: 5.08; prior picks only: 5.01.
M2, pit-size control: FFT of the rectified plaza gives a paver period of 10.5 c/m against 10.0 expected for 0.10 bricks, so the pit is 1.13-1.26. The spec evidence (pit = 6 paver lengths) gives 1.2. Sensitivity is -0.15 m of zp per +0.1 m of pit.
M3: CC003's 7 risers x 0.15 hold at the entrance. The fitted camera is 1.8 above the plaza, which fits a photographer on the A_W deck-end step.
items.what_would_settle: Confirm with one level reading or tape: plaza to the F1 sill at the west wing (expected 7.27-5.05 = 2.22 m) against the entrance (1.95).

items.question: Do the E ramp run end and the E-ramp juniper pit conflict?
items.decision: No change. Ramp 'Run' (edge 2, u 3.3-9.5) and PlanterE_Ramp/JuniperE_Ramp are consistent; both move with C (Y1-02).
items.methods:
M1: CE003 (24 mm, from the east, looking west along the ramp) shows the ramp-foot rail posts nearer the camera than the pit. So the pit is west of the ramp end, as in the model.
M2: CC001 is a 12 mm ultra-wide with uncorrected distortion, so its PnP overlay is unreliable. Geometrically, a NE-looking view puts the model pit (2.2 W and 2.5 S of the rail end) about 0.2 m to the right of the rail end and nearer the camera, which is the order the photo shows.

items.question: Room 101 door frame is 1.21 m from the S-wall jog corner (model 0.65). Which one moves: the jog/lobby E wall (X_JS) or the S4 door? Is the lobby really 4.5 m wide?
items.decision: The jog and the lobby walls move, and the door rule changes with them. The lobby is 3.76 m clear, not 4.5. In zone_c_v6.py: (a) Add LOBBY_X0, LOBBY_X1 = 12.82, 16.58. These are the clear faces, equal to the tower edges ±0.02 and to the storefront frame 12.82-16.58 already in BLD_C. P2 (12.35) and P3 (17.05) stay where they are, so rooms 108 and 101 are unchanged. The lobby side walls become 0.57 thick (x 12.25-12.82 and 16.58-17.15): on F1, make Room_S_12.35 and Room_S_17.05 (facade to HW0) thk 0.57, or add a 0.37 lining on the lobby side. Hall_S_West (F1) ends at x 12.82 (was 12.45). Hall_S_Jog becomes thk 0.57 with its W face at 16.58 (line at x 17.15, thickness to the west). Hall_S_East starts at 16.58. F1 lobby ceilings and fittings that reference P2±PART/2 or X_JS-PART/2 follow the new faces. F2+ room k09 uses the same faces (width 3.76; the tower windows at 13.72/15.66 are then centred). (b) DOOR_OFF = PART/2 + 0.60 + DOOR_W/2 = 1.195 (was 1.045). Every classroom door frame edge is then 0.60 from the board-wall plane, or 0.45 from the existing 0.15 Pilaster_BoardDoor. S4 frame = 17.75-18.74. World coordinates: lobby W face at the hall line (186.353, 2.844); lobby E face (190.110, 2.694); jog corner (190.161, 3.993); S4 frame W edge (191.331, 3.946).
items.methods: M1, CI002 ceiling grid (0.6 lay-in module, Hough lines in h002.npy): column seams at the storefront-head edge are at x 779/989/1195/1405/1619 px (210 px per 0.6 m), and the walls are at 636 and about 1942 px. That gives a clear width of 6.22-6.26 tiles = 3.73-3.76 m, matching the 3.76 storefront and the 3.8 tower. A 4.5 m lobby would be 7.5 tiles. M2, CI001 S-wall homography (round 1): the corner is 1.21±0.15 m from the S4 frame W edge. M3, door-to-board-plane distance from 5 measurements. CI019 door-wall homography (h019.py, dark frame 0.99x2.05) puts the frame 0.476 m from the pilaster face, consistent at 4 heights; with a pilaster about 0.13 the frame is 0.61 m from the board-wall plane. CK018 (h18) gives 0.61-0.68, CR012 0.57, CR016 0.54, verify2 0.66. Mean 0.60±0.05 (model 0.45). Combined: S4 frame W edge 17.15+0.60 = 17.75, so the corner is at 17.75-1.21 = 16.54±0.16, which agrees with the tower edge and the storefront at 16.58 and with the 3.76 width from the symmetric W face at 12.82. Rejected option, moving the door 0.56 E: it gives a 1.0 m door-to-board distance (measured 0.54-0.68) and does not explain the 3.76 m lobby.
items.error: lobby width ±0.06; lobby faces ±0.10 (W face position rests on the width plus tower symmetry); door offset ±0.05
items.confidence: medium-high (width, door rule), medium (W face position)
items.what_would_settle: A tape from the 108 (S2) frame E edge to the lobby W corner would confirm the W wall at 12.82 (predicted 1.17 m).

items.question: 103 door E frame edge to the E stair-front corner: 1.07 (round 1), 1.55 (round 2) or 1.46 (model). Settle STAIR_X / FRONT_E.
items.decision: The relative distance is 1.46 m, as in the model. Because the door rule changes (X0-05, DOOR_OFF 1.195, N5 frame 23.75-24.74), keep 1.46 by moving the front: FRONT_E = 26.20, so STAIR_X = 2.75. Set FLIGHT_W = 1.275 and keep WELL 0.20 (2*1.275+0.20 = 2.75). Apply the same STAIR_X to the W stair (FRONT_W = 3.20, mirrored stairs per owner). World coordinates: N5 frame E edge (198.546, 9.463); stair-front/N-wall corner (200.005, 9.405). If DOOR_OFF is not changed, keep FRONT_E 26.05 and FLIGHT_W 1.35.
items.methods: M1, CI012 N-wall homography (h012.py) from the 103 outer frame corners (490,995)/(1316,1062)/(1324,2640)/(590,2752) = 0.99x2.05. The blue/white corner at x 2262 maps to u 2.41, so the frame E edge is 1.42±0.07 from the corner. Self-checks: ceiling at 2.92 (expected 2.95-3.00), skirting at 0.078. The round-1 value 1.07 came from a single px/m on a strongly receding wall: the frame jambs measure 1757 vs 1578 px. M2, CC010 PnP (round 2, re-solved with cam.py): 1.55±0.10. Weighted mean 1.46±0.06. Shifting the N5/S5 control points by 0 to +0.25 m changes the CC010 residual only from 9.6 to 10.9 px, so CC010 gives the relative distance only. Its end-wall-referenced corner at 26.13-26.16 (STAIR_X 2.79-2.82) agrees with 26.20 within error.
items.confidence: medium-high (relative distance); medium (absolute FRONT_E, tied to X0-05)

items.question: F1 flight-2 underside and half-landing height (model LANDING 1.16, landing top 1.612, 11+11 risers): count the risers and fit the stair.
items.decision: zone_c_v6.py: RISER_H = STOREY/20.5 = 0.1610; BOTTOM_RISER = 0.5*RISER_H = 0.0805; TREAD = 0.31 (was 0.332). Flight 1 keeps RISERS = 11 (half bottom riser plus 10). Add RISERS2 = 10 for flight 2, and use it in stair_storey() flight 2 and in the closet soff() formula, which hard-codes RISERS. Landing top = 0.0805+10*0.161 = 1.690 (was 1.612). LANDING = 1.24, so y_b = h0+(COR-LANDING-10*TREAD) = h0+1.46: E stair foot y 9.76, landing edge 12.86, flight 2 top at y 10.07 (2.79 run). SOFFIT stays 0.08. The flight-2 underside at the exit-door N jamb (y 10.78) rises about +0.17, to about 2.69. Re-run the closet/exit-door clearance QA.
items.methods: Riser count. CC010 side profile of E flight 1 (x = FRONT_E face): risers at x 1275, 1344, 1419, 1497, 1572, 1647, 1731, 1809, 1887, 1969, plus a half step at about 2050, i.e. 10 full + 1 half = 11. Video 070704360 f68 (W stair flight 1 from its foot, nosing profile at 591/644/696/756/833/918/1034/1180/1373/1641 plus a bottom half step at about 1910): also 11. Flight 2 in CI014: tread lines at y 1861, 1761, 1655, 1544, 1425, 1308, 1180, 1042, 900, then the top riser to the F2 landing edge at about 790 (radiator behind the guard). That is 9 treads, so 10 risers. CI015 flight-2 W face shows 9 treads; the top is hidden by the hall ceiling edge, so it cannot decide. Geometry: CC010 sawtooth back-projected through the PnP camera (cam.py) onto x 26.05/26.20 gives treads 0.306/0.313 and 10 risers summing 1.58-1.62 (0.158-0.162 each). The landing comes out at 1.74 with the floor at 0.05-0.085 (z bias), so the landing is about 1.66-1.69. Foot at y 9.75-9.77 and landing edge at 12.82-12.88 (model 9.62/12.94). CI015 frontal flight-2 face: riser/tread = 72.5/136 = 0.533 (0.165/0.31). Consistency: 3.30 - 1.69 = 1.61 = 10 x 0.161. The model's 11 x 0.1535 does not fit the measured riser height. The landing rise (+0.078) and the steeper flight-2 soffit explain the Y0-n +0.09 and X0-01 2.57-2.71 residuals.
items.error: riser ±0.004, tread ±0.01, landing top ±0.03, flight-2 count ±0 above the bottom tread (the bottom one is only confirmed by the height balance)

items.question: Window head vs window beam: is the interior sill 1.15 with head 2.55, or does the beam soffit drop to 2.60?
items.decision: Keep the beam soffit at 2.70 (WindowBeam z C-0.20..C) and the 1.40 frame height. Raise the window 0.10. Art/Blender/Specs/BLD_C.json rows: F1 1.15, F2 4.45, F3 7.75, F4 11.05 (was 1.05/4.35/7.65/10.95). zone_c_v6.py WIN_SILL = 1.15 (WIN_H 1.40 unchanged), so the head is at 2.55, 0.15 below the beam. Any other generator that copies the row sills (c_shell_v6.py) must read the same values.
items.methods: M1, CK020 frontal R105 window wall: lining top at y 717, sill board at 1477 (760 px tall, 1031 wide, h/w 0.737), beam soffit edge at about 638. Strip/lining = 79/760 = 0.104, i.e. 0.15 m for a 1.40-1.45 lining, matching round 1's 0.15. M2, CI017 (R102, man 1.77 at the end wall, 655 px/m at his depth, wall about 0.12 m behind him): sill 1.14 and lining top 2.67 (the lining includes trim). M3, the C105 reference sheet: sill 1.10, head 2.55, beam 2.70. The facade sill of 1.05 is an exterior fit relative to an estimated FFL, so it is the weaker datum.

items.question: Does the C west stair continue above F3 (F3/F4 stair-hall video)?
items.decision: Yes. The W stair continues F3 to F4. In zone_c_v6.py build(), F2-F4 loop: west = k <= 4 (was k <= 3). Generate StairW for k < 4 with top_floor=(k == 3) (was k < 3, top_floor k == 2). ceilings(): W band for k < 4. On F4, plan(west_stair=True) removes F4_Teach_W_Front / F4_Door_Teach_W, and the F4 W end becomes the stair floor landing. StairW_F2_TopGuard moves to StairW_F3_TopGuard. Flag for the lore/owner list: this contradicts docs/reference/campus.md ('W stair F1-F3 only; F4 offices where the W stair would be'). The video shows what is physically there.
items.methods: Video 052716931. Door sign read at full 4K (t 7.5 s) as '302'. A continuous pan along one wall runs 302 door, bench, a second door (301), then the stair hall, which fixes F3 and the W end under the model numbering (S1 = k01). M1, f43-f54: two people walk down a flight from an upper landing and step off at the F3 floor. M2, f47-f48: a further sawtooth flight rises from that landing toward F4. Both show flights above F3.
items.confidence: high that flights exist above F3; low on the F4 arrival layout

items.question: Is the W stair dog-leg rotated 180 deg (mid-landings at the S, floor landing at the N) at F3?
items.decision: Not applied. Keep the model orientation for every storey: flight 1 on the hall-side lane rising S to N, mid-landing at the N, flight 2 on the end-wall lane rising N to S. Use the new constants from Y0-n.
items.methods: M1, F1 W stair: CI003 and video 070704360 f49-f72 show flight 1 on the hall-side lane rising S to N to a landing at the N, matching the model. E stair: CC010/CI015 show the same, and CI014 shows the F2 floor landing at the S end of flight 2. M2, video 052716931 at F3: the up-flight appears behind a floor-level guard and runs from the N floor up to an upper S landing, which suggests swapped lanes. A per-storey 180 deg swap cannot be built above a standard F1 to F2 dog-leg: the F2 floor over the F1 flight-1 N end would leave about 1.3 m headroom. So one of the two readings must be wrong.
items.confidence: medium for the F1-F2 orientation; low for F3 and above
items.what_would_settle: One photo or frame of the W stair at F2 or F3 looking N or S along the bay, showing at which end and on which lane the up-flight leaves the floor landing.

items.question: Size of the bulkhead box along the top of the board wall (102, 204).
items.decision: zone_c_v6.py fitout(): add bx('BoardBox', L-0.20, L, 0.30, D-0.60, C-0.19, C+0.01), painted to match the board wall behind it (sage on the sage part, white near the door, following BoardWall_Paint). It runs the full board wall from the door-corner pilaster (v 0.30) to the window-side pilaster (v D-0.60), not 0.30..D-0.50. Use it in the class-room fit-out (102, 204 and the rooms on the same pattern), not in R105.
items.methods: CI023 frontal board wall (R102). The box front face spans 506 to 610 px and the underside 610 to 632 px; the floor at the wall is at 2045 (skirting top 1998). Height, independent of scale: h/(C-h) = (104/1.035)/1413 with C = 2.90, so h = 0.19. With the wall span (5.75 m = 2941 px, 511 px/m) the box-wall junction is at 2.77, i.e. 0.13-0.20 below a 2.90-2.97 ceiling (2.5% scale error). Depth from the underside parallax (22 px, D 5.5 m, camera 1.4-1.7 m) is 0.18-0.24. The box ends against the window-side column in the left crop.
